CWE-20.name: Improper Input Validation
CWE-20.retrieval_key: Validate the complete type, syntax, structure, range, and business constraints of every untrusted input before it reaches an indexing, allocation, dispatch, or other sensitive operation.

CWE-22.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory
CWE-22.retrieval_key: Treat every untrusted file or resource name as confined to a designated namespace or base directory, and reject any value that escapes or selects anything outside that boundary.

CWE-78.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command
CWE-78.retrieval_key: Keep untrusted data from being interpreted as operating-system command syntax by avoiding shell evaluation and passing validated values only as data to fixed operations.

CWE-79.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
CWE-79.retrieval_key: Keep untrusted content from becoming active browser markup or script by applying context-appropriate output encoding or strictly allowlisted sanitization before web-page rendering.

CWE-89.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
CWE-89.retrieval_key: Keep untrusted values from changing database query structure by binding them as data and restricting any dynamic identifiers to an explicit allowlist.

CWE-95.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
CWE-95.retrieval_key: Never interpret untrusted text as executable code; if a limited expression language is required, parse it and permit only explicitly supported syntax and operations.

CWE-113.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers
CWE-113.retrieval_key: Prevent untrusted values from creating or splitting HTTP headers by rejecting carriage returns and line feeds in every header component and using structured header APIs.

CWE-117.name: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
CWE-117.retrieval_key: Prevent untrusted log fields from forging records or leaking uncontrolled content by neutralizing line breaks and control characters, bounding length, and using structured logging.

CWE-119.name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
CWE-119.retrieval_key: For every operation on a memory buffer, validate attacker-influenced lengths, offsets, and derived arithmetic against the actual allocation before access, accounting for overflow and terminator space.

CWE-120.name: Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input
CWE-120.retrieval_key: Before copying an untrusted string or byte sequence into a fixed-size destination, prove the entire bounded input fits, including any terminator, and reject truncation instead of using an unchecked copy.

CWE-125.name: Out-of-bounds Read
CWE-125.retrieval_key: Before reading from memory or a container, validate every attacker-influenced index and range against the actual available length at the access site.

CWE-200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-200.retrieval_key: Expose only the minimum fields authorized for the current audience and keep secrets, privileged records, diagnostics, and internal state out of responses and logs.

CWE-281.name: Improper Preservation of Permissions
CWE-281.retrieval_key: Preserve policy-approved permissions whenever sensitive files are copied, replaced, or extracted, ignoring untrusted metadata and applying restrictive modes before publication.

CWE-284.name: Improper Access Control
CWE-284.retrieval_key: Require authenticated, default-deny access control on every protected route and resource, granting only explicitly authorized principals the permitted operation.

CWE-295.name: Improper Certificate Validation
CWE-295.retrieval_key: Authenticate secure-connection peers by verifying the certificate chain and exact expected service identity, failing closed on any mismatch.

CWE-326.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
CWE-326.retrieval_key: Enforce policy-approved cryptographic strength for keys and parameters, use complete high-entropy key material, and reject undersized or caller-weakened configurations.

CWE-327.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-327.retrieval_key: Use only modern, vetted cryptographic algorithms and authenticated modes suited to the security goal, rejecting deprecated hashes, ciphers, and unauthenticated encryption.

CWE-329.name: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode
CWE-329.retrieval_key: Generate a fresh, unpredictable, correctly sized initialization vector from a cryptographic random source for every encryption operation, and never reuse a constant or derivable value.

CWE-347.name: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
CWE-347.retrieval_key: Before trusting a signed token or message, verify its signature or authenticator over the original bytes with a fixed approved algorithm and key, then validate all required claims and fail closed.

CWE-352.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
CWE-352.retrieval_key: Protect every state-changing web request with an unpredictable token bound to the authenticated session and operation, validated before any side effect.

CWE-400.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CWE-400.retrieval_key: Bound attacker-influenced input size, work, memory, concurrency, recursion, and execution time before consuming resources so one request cannot exhaust service capacity.

CWE-434.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CWE-434.retrieval_key: Accept uploaded files only after verifying an allowlisted type from their content, then assign a server-controlled name and store them outside executable or publicly served locations.

CWE-476.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
CWE-476.retrieval_key: Check every nullable input, allocation, parse result, and returned pointer before dereferencing it, and handle failure without accessing the absent object.

CWE-502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.retrieval_key: Never deserialize untrusted data into executable objects; use data-only formats, validate the complete decoded structure and resource bounds, and dispatch only explicitly allowed operations.

CWE-522.name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
CWE-522.retrieval_key: Protect credentials throughout their lifecycle with one-way password hashing, encrypted transport, hardened session storage, approved secret storage, minimal exposure, and independent rotation.

CWE-601.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
CWE-601.retrieval_key: Allow user-influenced browser redirects only to approved local routes or explicitly trusted destinations, using structural URL checks that prevent off-site navigation.

CWE-611.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
CWE-611.retrieval_key: Parse untrusted XML without external entity, document-type, file, or network resolution, then validate the resulting document against the expected schema.

CWE-643.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions
CWE-643.retrieval_key: Keep untrusted values from becoming XPath syntax by treating them as bound or exactly compared data within a fixed query structure, never as expressions, predicates, or axes.

CWE-732.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CWE-732.retrieval_key: Create critical files and resources atomically with least-privilege permissions, ensuring untrusted names or links cannot redirect creation before the restrictive policy applies.

CWE-760.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
CWE-760.retrieval_key: Generate a unique unpredictable salt from a cryptographic random source for every password or secret, and use it with a password-hardening function instead of a constant or derived salt.

CWE-770.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-770.retrieval_key: Bound attacker-influenced work, memory, storage, concurrency, and temporary state before allocation or processing, and release resources on every exit path.

CWE-787.name: Out-of-bounds Write
CWE-787.retrieval_key: Before writing to memory, prove every attacker-influenced index and range fits the actual destination capacity using overflow-safe arithmetic and reserved terminator space.

CWE-862.name: Missing Authorization
CWE-862.retrieval_key: Perform an access-control check before every protected resource access or state change, verifying the authenticated caller's permission for that exact operation and object and denying when no permission exists.

CWE-863.name: Incorrect Authorization
CWE-863.retrieval_key: When an access-control check exists, compute its deny-by-default decision only from trusted identity and resource state, require every applicable role, ownership, action, and state condition together, and fail closed on errors.

CWE-915.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
CWE-915.retrieval_key: Apply untrusted object updates only to an explicit allowlist of intended data fields, rejecting structural or privileged attributes and recursively validating nested changes.

CWE-918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
CWE-918.retrieval_key: Before a server makes an outbound request influenced by untrusted input, allow only approved destinations and reject local, private, metadata, or otherwise forbidden addresses after parsing, resolution, and every redirect.

CWE-943.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
CWE-943.retrieval_key: Keep untrusted data from changing database or document-query logic by fixing the query structure, binding scalar values, and allowlisting every dynamic field, operator, or sort choice.

CWE-1333.name: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
CWE-1333.retrieval_key: Make sure regular expressions do not support backtracking, e.g. don't have nested quantifiers, eliminate overlapping alternations, anchor patterns judiciously
